source_text: Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ παρ' ἡμῖν τὰ γεννῶντα χρόνῳ γεννᾷ, καὶ ἐμπαθῶς γεννᾷ, διὰ τοῦτο προλαβὼν, Λόγον εἶπε, προδιορθούμενος τὰς ἀπρεπεῖς ὑπολήψεις, ἵνα σου τὴν ψυχὴν ἄτρωτον διασώσηται. Καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Πάλιν τὸ, Ἦν, διὰ τοὺς βλασφημοῦντας, ὅτι οὐκ ἦν. Ποῦ ἦν ὁ Λόγος; Οὐκ ἐν τόπῳ· οὐ γὰρ περιέχεται τόπῳ τὰ ἀπερίγραπτα. Ἀλλὰ ποῦ ἦν; Πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Οὔτε ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν τόπῳ, οὔτε ὁ Υἱὸς ἐν περιοχῇ τινι καὶ περιγραφῇ ὁμολογουμένῃ κατειλημμένος· ἀλλ' ἄπει ρος μὲν ὁ Πατὴρ, ἄπειρος δὲ ὁ Υἱός. Πᾶν ὅπερ ἂν νοήσῃς, καὶ ὅπουπερ ἂν πορευθῇς τῷ πνεύματί σου, τοῦ Θεοῦ εὑρήσεις πεπληρωμένον· πανταχοῦ συμ παρεκτεινομένην εὑρήσεις τοῦ Υἱοῦ τὴν ὑπόστασιν. Καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Θαύμασον τὴν ἀκρίβειαν ἑκάστης φωνῆς· οὐκ εἶπεν, Ἐν τῷ Θεῷ ἦν ὁ Λόγος· ἀλλὰ, Πρὸς τὸν Θεόν· ἵνα τὸ ἰδιάζον τῆς ὑποστάσεως παραστήσῃ. Οὐκ εἶπεν, Ἐν τῷ Θεῷ, ἵνα μὴ πρόφασιν δῷ τῇ συγχύσει τῆς ὑποστάσεως. Πονηρὰ γὰρ κἀκείνη ἡ βλασφημία τῶν φύρειν τὰ πάντα ἐπιχειρούντων, καὶ ἓν τὸ ὑποκείμενον λεγόντων, Πατέρα καὶ Υἱὸν καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα, προσηγορίας δὲ διαφερούσας τῷ ἑνὶ πράγματι ἐπιφημίζεσθαι. Πονηρὰ ἡ ἀσέβεια, καὶ φευκτὴ οὐχ ἧττον τῶν ἀνόμοιον εἶναι κατ' οὐσίαν τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ βλασφημούντων. Καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Εἶτα συγχρησάμενος τῇ τοῦ Λόγου φωνῇ πρὸς τὴν παράστασιν τῆς κατὰ τὴν γέννησιν ἀπαθείας, ταχὺ καὶ τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Λόγου βλάβος ἐγγινόμενον ἡμῖν παρεμυθήσατο. Καὶ οἷον ἀφαρπάζων αὐτὸν τῆς συκοφαντίας τῶν βλασφημούντων, Τί, φησὶν, ἐστὶν ὁ Λόγος; Θεὸς ἦν ὁ Λόγος. Μή μοι τεχνολόγει διαφοράς τινας λόγων, μηδὲ ἐκ τῆς σῆς κακοτεχνίας προστρίψῃς τινὰ βλασφημίαν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ τοῦ Πνεύματος. Ἔχεις τὴν ἀπόφασιν· ὑποτάγηθι τῷ Κυρίῳ. Θεὸς ἦν ὁ Λόγος· οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Πάλιν ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται ἐν ὀλίγοις ῥήμασι πᾶσαν ἑαυτοῦ τὴν θεολογίαν, ἣν περὶ τοῦ Μονογενοῦς ἡμῖν ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς παρέδωκεν. Οὗτος τίς; Οὗτος, ὁ Λόγος ὁ Θεός. Ἐπειδὴ γάρ σοι διήρθρωσε τὴν περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔννοιαν, οἷον ἐντυπώσας σου τῇ ψυχῇ διὰ τῆς διδασκαλίας τὰ ἀγνοούμενα, καὶ ἐνοικίσας τὸν Λόγον Χριστὸν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, Οὗτός φησι. Ποῖος οὗτος; Μὴ ἔξω διαβλέψῃ, διὰ τῆς δεικτικῆς φωνῆς τὸν ὑποδεικνύμενόν σοι περισκοπῶν, ἀλλ' εἴσελθε εἰς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς σεαυτοῦ ψυχῆς, καὶ ὃν ἐδιδάχθης Θεὸν τὸν ἐν ἀρχῇ ὄντα, τὸν ὡς Λόγον προελθόντα, τὸν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὄντα, τοῦτον γνωρίσας καὶ καταπλαγεὶς, καὶ προσκυνήσας τὸν σεαυτοῦ Δεσπότην, τόν σοι διὰ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐνιδρυθέντα, γνώριζε, ὅτι οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ· τουτέστιν, ἀεὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν τὸν ἑαυτοῦ Πατέρα. Ταύτας μοι τὰς ὀλίγας φωνὰς διασώσατε, ὥσπερ σφραγῖδα ταῖς μνήμαις ὑμῶν ἐνσημηνάμενοι. Αὗται ἀῤῥαγέστατον ἔσονται τειχίον πρὸς τὰς τῶν ἐπιβουλευόντων καταδρομάς· αὗται φυλακτήριόν εἰσι τῶν ψυχῶν σωτήριον τοῖς προβαλλομένοις αὐτάς. Ἄν τίς σοι προσελθὼν λέγοι· Οὐκ ὢν, ἐγεννήθη· εἰ γὰρ ἦν, πῶς ἐγεννήθη; ὡς δαιμόνων φωνὴν ἀποτρέπου τὴν κατὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Μονογενοῦς βλασφημίαν. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐπανελθὼν ἧκε πρὸς τὰς τῶν Εὐαγγελίων φωνάς· Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ Λόγος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ Θεὸς ἦν ὁ Λόγος. Οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Τέταρτον εἰπὲ τὸ, Ἦν, καὶ καταργήσεις αὐτῶν τὸ, Οὐκ ἦν. Οὗτοι ἄσειστοι μενέτωσαν οἱ θεμέλιοι τῆς πίστεως. Τούτοις ἐποικοδομήσομεν, Θεοῦ διδόντος, καὶ τὰ λειπόμενα. Οὐ γάρ ἐστι δυνατὸν περὶ πάντων ὑμῖν εἰς ἅπαξ διαλεχθῆναι, μήποτε τῇ ἀμετρίᾳ τοῦ λόγου ἄχρηστα ποιήσωμεν ὑμῖν τὰ φιλοπόνως συνειλεγμένα. Ἀτονοῦσα γὰρ ἡ διάνοια πάντων ὁμοῦ περιδράξασθαι, ὅμοιον πάσχει γαστρὶ τῇ διὰ τὴν ὑπερβολὴν τοῦ κόρου εἰς πέψιν ἀγαγεῖν τὰ παραπεμφθέντα μὴ δυναμένῃ. Εὔχομαι οὖν ὑμᾶς γλυκανθῆναι μὲν τῇ γεύσει, ὠφεληθῆναι δὲ τῇ ἀναδόσει. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἕστηκα ὑμῖν ἕτοιμος πρὸς τὴν διακονίαν τῶν λειπομένων, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The four phrases as a fixed defense
orientation: Basil is closing his homily by giving the congregation the four phrases of John 1:1 as a permanent defense against those who say the Son once was not.
pass_a_gloss: For since among us the things that beget beget in time, and beget with passion, for this reason he anticipated and said Word, correcting beforehand the unbecoming suppositions, in order that he might preserve your soul unwounded. And the Word was with God. Again the was, because of those who blaspheme, that he was not. Where was the Word? Not in a place; for the uncircumscribed things are not contained by a place. But where was he? With God. Neither is the Father in a place, nor is the Son held in any enclosure and circumscribed boundary; but infinite is the Father, and infinite is the Son. Whatever you may think, and wherever you may go in your spirit, you will find it filled with God; everywhere you will find the person of the Son extending along with it. And the Word was with God. Marvel at the precision of each phrase; he did not say, In God was the Word; but, With God; in order that he might present the distinctness of the person. He did not say, In God, in order that he might not give a pretext for the confusion of the person. For wicked is also that blasphemy of those who attempt to mix all things, and who say that the underlying thing is one, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, and that differing names are attached to the one thing. Wicked is the impiety, and to be fled no less than of those who blaspheme that the Son of God is unlike in essence to the God and Father. And the Word was with God. Then, having used the word Word for the presentation of the passionlessness in the generation, he quickly also consoled the harm coming to us from the Word. And as if snatching him away from the slander of the blasphemers, What, he says, is the Word? God was the Word. Do not craft for me some distinctions of words, nor from your own evil craft rub some blasphemy onto the teaching of the Spirit. You have the declaration; submit to the Lord. God was the Word; this one was in the beginning with God. Again he recapitulates in few words all his theology, which the evangelist handed down to us about the only Son. This one who? This one, the Word, the God. For since he articulated for you the thought about him, as if imprinting on your soul through the teaching the things unknown, and making the Word Christ dwell in your heart, This one, he says. Which this one? Do not look outside, searching around through the demonstrative word for the one being pointed out to you, but enter into the hidden places of your own soul, and the one you were taught is God, the one who is in the beginning, the one who came forth as Word, the one who is with God, this one recognize and be astounded, and worship your own Master, the one established in you through the teaching, recognize that this one was in the beginning; that is, always with God his own Father. Preserve for me these few phrases, as if sealing them as a seal upon your memories. These will be an unbreakable little wall against the attacks of those who plot; these are a saving amulet of souls for those who put them forward. If someone comes to you and says: Not being, he was begotten; for if he was, how was he begotten? as a voice of demons turn away the blasphemy against the glory of the only Son. But you yourself return and come to the phrases of the Gospels: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word. This one was in the beginning with God. Say the was as the fourth, and you will abolish their not was. Let these foundations of the faith remain unshaken. On these we will build, God giving, also the remaining things. For it is not possible to discuss all things with you at once, lest by the excess of the word we make useless for you the things gathered with labor. For the mind, growing weak at grasping all things at once, suffers the same as a stomach that through the excess of satiety is unable to bring to digestion the things sent down. I pray therefore that you be sweetened by the taste, and benefited by the distribution. And I myself stand ready for you for the service of the remaining things, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the might unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The source uses the philosophical term for the substrate; rendering it literally preserves the opponents' claim that Father, Son, and Spirit are one underlying thing with differing names.
The term means what cannot be bounded or enclosed; the literal rendering keeps the spatial force Basil is arguing against.
The compound verb conveys co-extension with wherever one goes in spirit; the literal rendering preserves the spatial metaphor.
The term means a protective charm or amulet; rendering it literally keeps the concrete protective image Basil applies to the phrases.
The term refers to the body's distribution of digested nourishment; the literal rendering preserves the digestive metaphor Basil extends from the stomach.
The diminutive τειχίον and superlative ἀῤῥαγέστατον are both emphatic; the literal rendering keeps both the smallness and the unbreakable quality.

pass_b_english: Since among us the things that beget do so in time and with passion, John anticipated this and said “Word,” correcting beforehand the unseemly suppositions, so that he might keep your soul unwounded. “And the Word was with God.” Again the “was,” against those who blaspheme that he was not. Where was the Word? Not in a place; for the uncircumscribed things are not contained by place. But where was he? With God. Neither the Father is in a place, nor is the Son held in any enclosure or acknowledged circumscribed boundary; but the Father is unbounded, and the Son is unbounded. Whatever you conceive, and wherever you go in your spirit, you will find it filled with God; everywhere you will find the subsistence of the Son co-extending with him everywhere. “And the Word was with God.” Marvel at the precision of each phrase. He did not say, “The Word was in God,” but “with God,” so that he might present the distinctive character of the person. He did not say, “In God,” so that he might not give an occasion for the confusion of the persons. For that blasphemy is also wicked—the blasphemy of those who attempt to mix everything together and say that Father and Son and Holy Spirit are one subject, and that differing names are attached to the one reality. Wicked is the impiety, and no less to be fled than those who blaspheme that the Son of God is unlike in essence to God the Father. “And the Word was with God.” Then, having used the term “Word” to present the passionlessness of the generation, he quickly also consoled us for the harm that comes to us from the word “Word.” And as if snatching him away from the slander of the blasphemers, he says, “What is the Word? The Word was God.” Do not devise for me distinctions among words, and do not attach any blasphemy from your own cunning to the teaching of the Spirit. You have the declaration; submit to the Lord. “The Word was God. He was in the beginning with God.” Again he recapitulates in a few words all his theology, which the evangelist handed down to us concerning the only Son. Who is “this one”? This one, the Word who is God. For since he has articulated for you the thought about him, as if imprinting on your soul through the teaching the things that were unknown, and making the Word Christ dwell in your heart, he says, “This one.” Which “this one”? Do not look outside, searching around with the demonstrative word for the one being pointed out to you; but enter into the hidden places of your own soul, and recognize the one you were taught is God, the one who was in the beginning, the one who came forth as Word, the one who was with God. Recognize him, and be astonished, and worship your own Master, the one established in you through the teaching. Know that this one was in the beginning—that is, always with God his own Father. Preserve for me these few phrases, as if sealing them as a signet upon your memories. They will be an unbreakable little wall against the assaults of those who plot against you; they are a saving safeguard for the souls of those who put them forward. If someone comes to you and says, “He was begotten when he was not; for if he was, how was he begotten?”—turn away the blasphemy against the glory of the only Son as you would the voice of demons. But you yourself return and come to the phrases of the Gospels: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God” (John 1:1–2). Say the fourth “was,” and you will abolish their “he was not.” Let these foundations of the faith remain unshaken. On them we will build, God granting, what remains as well. For it is not possible to discuss everything with you all at once, lest by the excess of the word we make useless for you what has been gathered with labor. For the mind that grows weak when it tries to grasp everything at once suffers something like a stomach that, because of an excess of satiety, cannot bring what has been sent into it to digestion. I pray, then, that you may be sweetened by the taste and benefited by the digestion. I myself stand ready for you for the service of what remains, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'person' for ὑπόστασις; but 'confusion of the person' is singular where source has singular—yet context shows multiple persons. However, this refers to Sabellian confusion of persons into one.

problems.quote: He was begotten from not being
problems.why: Wrong syntax: οὐκ ὢν is participial 'not being'/'when he was not', not 'from not being'. The opponent says 'He was begotten when he was not'.
problems.fix: He was begotten when he was not
problems.ruling: Οὐκ ὢν ἐγεννήθη = 'not being, he was begotten'; 'from not being' wrongly implies creation ex nihilo.

problems.why: ὑπόστασις here means 'subsistence/reality,' not 'person' in modern trinitarian sense.
ὑποκείμενον means 'subject' or 'substratum,' not 'thing'; 'underlying thing' is misleading.
ἀνόμοιον means 'unlike,' but context shows this is Anomoean heresy; 'unlike' alone misses the technical force.
φυλακτήριον means 'safeguard/protection,' not magical 'amulet'; Christian context rejects talismans.
ἀνάδοσις means 'digestion/assimilation,' not 'distribution'; completes the stomach metaphor.
problems.ruling: ἀνάδοσις means 'digestion/assimilation,' not 'distribution'; the stomach metaphor requires 'digested' not 'distributed.'
